title: SOP Generation - SIPOC
subtitle: Your business relies on people remembering how to do things. When someone leaves or is
useWhen: absent, quality drops. You spend time explaining the same process repeatedly instead of running the business.
howToUse: SIPOC is a Six Sigma process mapping tool that defines a process across five elements: Suppliers (who provides inputs), Inputs (what is needed to start), Process (the steps in sequence), Outputs (what is produced), Customers (who receives the output). Used as the structure for a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), it ensures every process is fully documented not just the steps, but the context, the handoffs, and the success criteria. AI can generate a first-draft SOP for any process you describe in plain language.
steps: Describe the process in plain language first don't try to structure it as you describe it.
After AI generates the SOP, walk through it physically and correct any gaps.
Assign a process owner, one person responsible for keeping the SOP current.

Review all SOPs every six months or after any significant process change. Turn the process in your head into a document anyone can follow The most valuable line in any SOP is the Quality Check column how do you know each step was done correctly? Most SOPs document what to do but not how to verify it was done right. Adding one quality signal per step is the difference between a document that is followed and one that is ignored. PRO TIP
origin: Six Sigma methodology — SIPOC tool, widely used since 1980s
promptBody:
I PROMPT — COPY & PASTE READY
Act as an operations consultant specialising in SOP documentation.
Process to document     :  [NAME AND DESCRIBE THE PROCESS]
Who performs it             :  [ROLE AND EXPERIENCE LEVEL]
Tools and systems used :  [SOFTWARE, PLATFORMS, RESOURCES]
How often it runs            :  [DAILY / WEEKLY / PER PROJECT]
Generate a complete SOP using the SIPOC structure:
SIPOC OVERVIEW:
→ → → →
Suppliers  Inputs  Process Steps  Outputs  Customers
FULL SOP:
Purpose   :  Why this process exists
Scope       :  What is and is not included
Owner      :  Who is responsible for this process
Steps        :  Numbered steps with decision points noted
Quality     :  How to know each step was done correctly
Errors       :  Common mistakes and how to avoid them
Review     :  When and how this SOP should be updated
